steps: Check for shipping damage; confirm the hardware kit (conversion kit, rock wool, remote, batteries, screen guidelines).
Detach from pallet; use the corner leveling bolts (½" of adjustment) to plumb the unit in its final position.
Pipe to code, manual shut-off (T-handle in MA). Test for leaks with soap solution — never a flame.
Swap burner injectors and follow the conversion kit; fit the conversion notice plate.
Burner switch to REMOTE, transmitter off; Mode then Up/Down to choose IPI or CPI.
Connect the pair of 3" flex liners to the termination cap; seal and clamp.
Set the insert, fit backer plate / surround overlay, install the chosen log set.
Purge the line, verify pilot flames engulf the sensor, confirm ignition at HI.

items: Small pilot flame → poor rectification and burner outages
Little change in flame between HI and LO
Not enough gas for multiple appliances → nuisance outages or surges

items: Permanent valve damage → full appliance shutdown

Sooting from flame impingement / wrong fuel-air mix

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
This insert runs on its remote control. For a normal start:

  1. Set the Burner Switch to OFF. Wait five (5) minutes to clear out any gas.
  2. Then smell for gas all around the fireplace area, including next to the floor — some gas is heavier than air and settles there. If you smell gas, stop. Do not light any appliance. Follow "If you smell gas" in "Safety around the unit."
  3. Set the Burner Switch to REMOTE (it's in the right-side firebox compartment).
  4. Press the remote's Power button once. The burner ignites at the HI setting.
  5. If the fireplace will not operate, follow "To turn off the gas to the fireplace" below and call your service technician or gas supplier.
  6. Let it run — adjust flame height from the remote once it's lit.
Use only your hand to push in or turn the gas control knob. Never use tools. If the knob will not push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it — call a qualified technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.

To turn off the gas to the fireplace

  1. Set the remote thermostat to its lowest setting.
  2. Set the Burner Switch to OFF.
  3. Disconnect electric power to the fireplace if service is to be performed.
First few hours: a faint odor as the metal and finishes cure is normal and temporary. Open a window and let fresh air move through the room.

The glass will fog

A little condensation appears on the glass every time you light it. It clears on its own as the glass warms up.

After a long shut-off, the first ignition takes a moment while air purges from the gas line. That's expected.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The hand-held transmitter and the fireplace are paired at the factory, so it should just work once batteries are in.

The buttons

  • Power — turns the burner on (ignites at HI) and off.
  • Up / Down — flame height, and toggles options inside a mode.
  • Mode — steps through manual, thermostat and timer functions, and (with the display off) selects the pilot mode.
Thermostat warning: set thermostatically, the appliance can fire on its own. It may be very hot even when the burner looks off. Keep the remote where children can't reach it.

Lost the pairing? It can be re-synchronized — that procedure is in the full manual (remote control section).

sounds.title: That sound or smell is probably normal
sounds.html:
Creaking and pinging

Cast iron and steel expand and contract as they heat and cool. The ticks and creaks you hear are that natural thermal movement — not a fault.

A low hum

The optional blower fan hums quietly on its low setting and gets a little louder as the fan speeds up with forced air.

A faint odor early on

During the first stages of use it's normal to smell the finishes curing under heat. Promote fresh-air circulation nearby and it passes.

When to stop and call: a strong gas smell is different. If you smell gas, do not light any appliance, do not touch any electrical switch, and do not use any phone in your building. Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone or from outside the house. If you cannot reach your gas supplier, call the fire department. The full steps are in "Safety around the unit."

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Use a dedicated fireplace-glass cleaner or warm water on the cooled glass.

Don't skip it. If residue is left to bake on, it can permanently etch and discolor the glass — that's not covered by warranty.

Handling

  • The glass can shatter if struck — always handle it with care.
  • Only remove the glass for service, never while the unit is hot.
  • Make sure it's fully cooled before you clean it.

modes.title: Burner switch & pilot modes
modes.html:
Burner switch

ONburners only · ignite at last flame level
REMOTEall features available
OFFburner won't operate

Pilot modes

CPI (continuous): the pilot stays lit for up to 7 days. With no call for heat in that window it shuts off and falls back to IPI. Good for tough draft conditions.

IPI (on demand): the pilot lights just before the main burner each time and goes out after each heat cycle — less gas used at idle.

power.title: Power & batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on 120 V house current, with battery backup so it still lights in an outage.

Backup (IFC box)4 × AA
Remote transmitter3 × AAA
Don't store the AA backups permanently in the box — it can corrode. Put them in when you expect to need backup.

The optional accent lamp won't work during a power loss — that's normal, the burner still will on battery backup.

safety.title: Safety around the unit
safety.html:
• The appliance can be very hot even when the burner looks off, especially in thermostat mode — keep children away.
  • Keep the remote out of children's reach.
  • The glass may shatter if struck — handle with care.
  • A safety screen barrier reduces burn risk at the glass. If it's ever damaged, replace it before using the fireplace.
  • Do not use the fireplace if any part of it has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

If you smell gas

Fire or explosion hazard. Failure to follow safety warnings exactly could result in serious injury, death, or property damage.
  • Do not try to light any appliance.
  • Extinguish any open flame.
  • Open windows.
  • Do not touch any electrical switch. Do not use any phone in your building.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone or from outside the house. Follow the gas supplier's instructions.
  • If you cannot reach your gas supplier, call the fire department.
Massachusetts: a carbon-monoxide detector must be installed in the same room as the appliance.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
To the original retail purchaser, from date of purchase:

Cast iron, steel, firebox5 years
Burner, firebox panels2 years
Enamel finish2 years

Commonly voids coverage

  • Installation not per these instructions or local code
  • Unauthorized modification or repair
  • Misuse, or damage in transit
This is a summary. The full warranty terms and exclusions are in the official PDF.

specInput.title: Input rates
specInput.html:
NG max / min40,000 / 10,000 BTU/hr
LP max / min40,000 / 8,700 BTU/hr

Rated efficiency (CSA P.4.1-15): 63.67% on propane. Orifice / injector sizing changes on fuel conversion — see the conversion kit.

Note: the efficiency label (p. 2) gives the natural-gas efficiency as 62.29%; the specifications table (p. 4) gives 61.29%.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas4.0 – 7.0 in. WC
Propane12.0 – 14.0 in. WC

Measure at the inlet pressure tap with the appliance running. An external regulator is required for propane.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
Natural gas1.10 – 3.8 in. WC
Propane2.9 – 11.0 in. WC

Outside this band you'll see the faults listed under "Gas pressure faults." Pilot flames should be blue at the hood with traces of yellow at the edges, projecting ~1" and fully engulfing the top ¼" of the sensor.

specFirebox.title: Minimum fireplace cavity
specFirebox.html:
Inside height24"
Inside width23½" (at 16½" depth)
Inside depth16½"
Opening H × W24" × 33¾"

For an existing solid-fuel masonry or factory-built fireplace. Front leveling bolts are reachable through the side compartments; tip the firebox forward for the rear bolts.

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Vent through the chimney with a pair of 3" flexible aluminum liners listed for gas, to an approved termination cap.

Min liner diameter3"
Max vent height35 ft

In high wind or downdraft locations, increasing vent height or fitting a high-wind cap can resolve nuisance outages.

specClear.title: Clearances
specClear.html:
Measured from the finished floor of the fireplace opening.

Hearth protection (raised 6"+)0"
Top trim from hearth37"

Hearth-protection depth requirements reduce as the unit is raised off the floor. Mantel clearance follows the baseline chart in the manual (Fig. 6). Maintain combustible clearances throughout.

The lighting drawer gained the p. 51 label's five-minute wait, its stop lines (gas smell; a unit that will not operate), the gas-control-knob warning and the turn-off steps.
